> **Note:** The `jjhistostats()` function is designed primarily for use within **jamovi's GUI** (`JJStatsPlot` → `Distribution` → `Histogram`). The R calls below demonstrate every option and feature reproducibly.

# Histogram (`jjhistostats`)

## Overview

`jjhistostats` creates single-variable, multi-variable, and grouped histograms with optional one-sample location inference (`ggstatsplot`), publication-ready density/mean overlays (`ggpubr`), distribution diagnostics (density, Q-Q, and ECDF plots), severity-ranked clinical/statistical warnings, and plain-language clinical interpretation.

Four one-sample statistical families are supported when **Statistical results** (`resultssubtitle = TRUE`) is enabled:

- **Parametric (`"parametric"`)**: One-sample Student *t*-test with exact Hedges' *g* and noncentral-*t* confidence intervals.
- **Nonparametric (`"nonparametric"`)**: One-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank test with rank-biserial correlation *r* (disclosing continuity-corrected normal approximation at small *n*, pseudomedian symmetry assumptions, and exact zero-tie exclusions).
- **Robust (`"robust"`)**: Bootstrap-*t* test on a symmetric trimmed mean (`WRS2` two-sided; Phipson–Smyth one-sided with `B = 2000`, zero-exceedance floor patching, and zero-Winsorized-variance guards).
- **Bayesian (`"bayes"`)**: Bayesian one-sample *t*-test (`BayesFactor`) with user-configurable Cauchy prior scale `bfprior`, overflow-safe log-scale directional Bayes factors, and unconstrained posterior credible intervals.

## Datasets Used in This Guide

| Dataset | N | Key Features | Primary Use |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `jjhistostats_test` | 150 | `age_years`, `tumor_size_mm`, `bmi`, `psa_level`, `hemoglobin`, `treatment`, `disease_stage` | Basic, multi-variable, styling, and grouped examples |
| `jjhistostats_labvalues` | 120 | `glucose`, `cholesterol`, `triglycerides`, `creatinine`, `patient_group` | `lab_values` preset, parametric & Bayesian tests |
| `jjhistostats_pathology` | 130 | `ki67_index`, `mitotic_count`, `tumor_cellularity`, `tumor_grade`, `organ` | `pathology_scores` preset with unit bin width |
| `jjhistostats_skewed` | 100 | `cea`, `ca199`, `afp`, `crp`, `cancer_type` | `biomarkers` preset, nonparametric & robust tests |
| `jjhistostats_grouped` | 180 | `age_years`, `biomarker_level`, `response_value`, `treatment`, `disease_stage` | Grouped histograms and faceted `ggpubr` plots |
| `jjhistostats_bimodal` | 140 | `age_bimodal`, `tumor_burden`, `population` | Distribution diagnostics (density, Q-Q, ECDF) & Shapiro–Wilk |
| `jjhistostats_small` | 25 | `age`, `measurement`, `score`, `group` | Small-sample and small-group edge cases |

---

## 1. Basic & Multi-Variable Histograms

By default, all 13 boolean display/testing checkboxes are `FALSE`, producing a fast, purely descriptive histogram with automatic bin width $(\max(x) - \min(x)) / \sqrt{N_{\text{finite}}}$.

```{r basic-descriptive}
data(jjhistostats_test)

res_basic <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_test,
  dep = "age_years"
)
res_basic$plot
```

Selecting multiple continuous variables stacks them vertically with automatically scaled height (`1.15 * length(dep) * plotheight`).

```{r multi-variable}
res_multi <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_test,
  dep = c("age_years", "tumor_size_mm", "bmi"),
  centralityline = TRUE,
  resultssubtitle = TRUE,
  showInterpretation = TRUE
)
res_multi$plot
```

---

## 2. Clinical Presets

Four presets configure statistical defaults for common pathology and laboratory workflows while preserving any explicit non-default option you pass:

- `"lab_values"`: parametric, centrality line, statistical subtitle, Bayes factor caption, clinical interpretation.
- `"biomarkers"`: nonparametric Wilcoxon, centrality line, statistical subtitle, clinical interpretation.
- `"patient_chars"`: parametric, centrality line, statistical subtitle, interpretation off.
- `"pathology_scores"`: nonparametric, unit manual bin width (`binwidth = 1.0`), centrality line, clinical interpretation.

```{r clinical-presets}
data(jjhistostats_labvalues)
data(jjhistostats_pathology)

res_lab <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_labvalues,
  dep = "glucose",
  clinicalPreset = "lab_values"
)

res_path <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_pathology,
  dep = "mitotic_count",
  clinicalPreset = "pathology_scores"
)
res_path$plot
```

---

## 3. One-Sample Statistical Tests & Directionality

Enable `resultssubtitle = TRUE` and `enableOneSampleTest = TRUE` to test against a clinically meaningful reference threshold (`test.value`) rather than `0`.

### Parametric one-sided test with Bayes factor caption

```{r parametric-one-sided}
res_param <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_labvalues,
  dep = "glucose",
  typestatistics = "parametric",
  resultssubtitle = TRUE,
  enableOneSampleTest = TRUE,
  test.value = 100,
  alternative = "greater",
  conf.level = 0.90,
  bf.message = TRUE,
  bfprior = 0.707,
  digits = 3,
  seed = 20250101
)
res_param$plot
```

### Nonparametric (Wilcoxon signed-rank) & Robust (trimmed-mean bootstrap-*t*)

```{r nonparametric-and-robust}
data(jjhistostats_skewed)

res_np <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_skewed,
  dep = "crp",
  typestatistics = "nonparametric",
  resultssubtitle = TRUE,
  enableOneSampleTest = TRUE,
  test.value = 5.0,
  alternative = "greater"
)

res_rob <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_skewed,
  dep = "ca199",
  typestatistics = "robust",
  trimlevel = 0.15,
  resultssubtitle = TRUE,
  enableOneSampleTest = TRUE,
  test.value = 37.0,
  alternative = "two.sided",
  conf.level = 0.95,
  seed = 42
)
res_rob$plot
```

### Bayesian one-sample *t*-test

```{r bayesian-test}
res_bayes <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_labvalues,
  dep = "cholesterol",
  typestatistics = "bayes",
  bfprior = 1.0,
  resultssubtitle = TRUE,
  enableOneSampleTest = TRUE,
  test.value = 200,
  alternative = "less",
  conf.level = 0.95,
  seed = 42
)
res_bayes$plot
```

---

## 4. Grouped Analysis, Aesthetics, Labels & Theme

Specify `grvar` to create faceted per-group histograms (`plot2`), and customize bin width, colors, centrality lines, labels, dimensions, and theme.

```{r grouped-and-styled}
data(jjhistostats_grouped)

res_grouped <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_grouped,
  dep = "biomarker_level",
  grvar = "treatment",
  typestatistics = "nonparametric",
  resultssubtitle = TRUE,
  centralityline = TRUE,
  centralitytype = "nonparametric",
  centralitylinecolor = "#D55E00",
  centralitylinewidth = 1.5,
  centralitylinetype = "dotted",
  changebinwidth = TRUE,
  binwidth = 5.0,
  binfill = "#56B4E9",
  bincolor = "#003366",
  binalpha = 0.65,
  xlab = "Biomarker concentration (ng/mL)",
  title = "Biomarker Distribution by Treatment Arm",
  caption = "ClinicoPath grouped histogram example",
  plotwidth = 650,
  plotheight = 450,
  originaltheme = TRUE
)
res_grouped$plot2
```

Custom subtitles are displayed when `resultssubtitle = FALSE`:

```{r custom-subtitle}
res_sub <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_test,
  dep = "hemoglobin",
  resultssubtitle = FALSE,
  title = "Baseline Hemoglobin",
  subtitle = "Descriptive cohort distribution (no hypothesis test)",
  xlab = "Hemoglobin (g/dL)"
)
res_sub$plot
```

---

## 5. Publication-Ready `ggpubr` Plots & Distribution Diagnostics

When `ggpubrAddDensity = TRUE`, both `ggpubrPlot` and `ggpubrPlot2` automatically plot bars on the probability-density scale (`y = "density"`, `ylab = "Density"`) so bars and density curves share the exact same axis.

```{r ggpubr-and-diagnostics}
data(jjhistostats_bimodal)

res_diag <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_grouped,
  dep = "response_value",
  grvar = "disease_stage",
  addGGPubrPlot = TRUE,
  ggpubrPalette = "#0073C2FF",
  ggpubrAddDensity = TRUE,
  ggpubrAddMean = TRUE,
  addDistributionDiagnostics = TRUE,
  ggpubrDensityColor = "#009E73",
  ggpubrShowQQ = TRUE,
  ggpubrShowECDF = TRUE,
  showInterpretation = TRUE
)
res_diag$ggpubrPlot
res_diag$densityPlot
res_diag$qqPlot
res_diag$ecdfPlot
```

---

## 6. Edge Cases & Built-in Safety Guards

`jjhistostats` includes explicit clinical and numerical guards for small samples, missing grouping values, `n < 3` subgroups, constant values, and heavy ties in the trimmed core.

```{r edge-cases}
data(jjhistostats_small)

# Small sample (n = 25) and small groups (< 10): surfaces advisory warnings in `todo`
res_small <- jjhistostats(
  data = jjhistostats_small,
  dep = "score",
  grvar = "group",
  typestatistics = "nonparametric",
  resultssubtitle = TRUE
)

# Subgroup with n = 2 refuses statistical subtitle rather than collapsing Hedges' g to 0
df_tiny <- data.frame(
  v = c(1:10, 20, 25),
  g = factor(c(rep("Adequate", 10), "Tiny", "Tiny"))
)
res_tiny <- jjhistostats(
  data = df_tiny,
  dep = "v",
  grvar = "g",
  typestatistics = "parametric",
  resultssubtitle = TRUE
)
res_tiny$plot2
```
